title: Dunlo: A Study Companion for Khan Academy
subtitle: A useful session today. A clearer next step tomorrow.
executiveShort: Dunlo turns a Khan Academy goal into a useful study session. Its BACKTRACK engine investigates difficult steps, connects focused help to fresh practice, and builds a personal reviewer that gives learners a reason to return.

sections.name: Executive Summary
paragraphs: A learner can spend time studying and still face three unanswered questions: What should I practise now? Why does this step fail? What should I revisit tomorrow? Dunlo is a study companion for Khan Academy that connects those decisions into a manageable routine.

Learners start from a supported Khan activity, a shared study pack, their quiz topics, or a short mathematics challenge. Dunlo prepares a finite session using the goal, available time, and earlier work. Learners can learn first, practise, rehearse a quiz, or revisit a saved skill. Personal notes become editable, source-linked cards.

When a step becomes difficult, Dunlo’s recovery engine investigates a possible obstacle. Interactive explanations make the mathematics visible: changing a factor pair shows why its product can match while its sum fails. Official Khan video segments and matched exercises provide relevant support. Fresh independent problems then check what the learner can apply. A reviewer and note to future self make returning easier.

The demonstration connects nine destinations across mathematics, chemistry and physics, supported Khan activities, shared pack links, and same-screen study turns. A teacher workspace connects class goals, Khan assignment evidence, and useful follow-up actions.

With UP Manila’s endorsement, we propose a November 2026–March 2027 pilot involving 80–120 learners across 2–3 cohorts. It will test retained success on current tasks, repeated relevant Khan use, voluntary return, teacher effort, and actual costs. The wider ambition is a reusable study routine that educators and learners can carry across reviewed learning goals.

sections.name: Needs Assessment
paragraphs: The problem is the work between lessons: choosing a useful next task, understanding a specific mistake, and remembering what needs another look. These decisions can consume a learner’s study window or leave the same misunderstanding unresolved.

For x² + 7x + 12 = 0, a learner who answers 3 and 4 may need to examine how factors become solutions. Someone who answers 2 and 6 may need to examine the pair’s sum and product. Sending both to the same broad review misses an opportunity for more useful support. A teacher managing a shared lesson also needs to see who needs which step next.

Dunlo starts with secondary mathematics learners preparing for current class work or quizzes, including learners who are learning ahead and those who need recovery. Shared packs connect the class goal to personal support; the reviewer carries useful work into the next session.

Khan Academy already has a substantial Philippine presence. DepEd reported more than 711,000 learner-beneficiaries across over 2,700 public schools in January 2026. Our opportunity is to help learners make relevant, repeated use of that resource through an everyday study routine.

Before the school cycle, walkthroughs with 10–15 learners and discussions with 3–5 teachers will examine actual study decisions, wrong answers, language needs, device access, and acceptable teacher effort. Those findings will shape the first packs, explanations, and class schedule. Access barriers and requests for human help will remain part of the implementation record.

sections.name: Business Principles & Financials
paragraphs: Dunlo’s value is a repeatable study-and-teaching routine: reviewed packs, focused Khan support, a personal reviewer, and a practical way for educators to act on current learning needs. Core learner access remains free.

Our PHP 100,000 implementation scenario allocates PHP 24,000 to learning design and mathematics review; PHP 18,000 to access support; PHP 18,000 to evaluation; PHP 16,000 to school deployment; PHP 8,000 to product operations; PHP 8,000 to teacher onboarding and replication; PHP 3,000 to recruitment content; and PHP 5,000 to contingency. This is a planning allocation for implementation, separate from any team award. Spending will follow approved grant terms and actual quotations.

At 80–120 enrolled learners, that scenario equals approximately PHP 833–1,250 in planned cash per enrollee, including setup. We will also record staff and volunteer hours, recurring support, and the cost of adding a reviewed pack. Cost per documented learning outcome will use actual outcomes and expenditure.

The continuation hypothesis is institutional or philanthropic support for content review, teacher onboarding, access, and maintenance. Schools, university extension programmes, and education partners would support implementation services; learners would not be charged for Khan content. Conversations with budget owners will test the proposed service, decision process, and evidence required for renewal.

By March, the handover should identify a responsible maintenance owner, recurring costs, a reusable educator kit, and a credible funding route. Product growth should follow demonstrated usefulness and a support model that another institution can sustain.

sections.name: Innovation
paragraphs: Dunlo makes one study session improve the next. Its distinctive mechanism is an answer-sensitive recovery route embedded inside ordinary learning, quiz preparation, and personal review.

Consider x² + 7x + 12 = 0. Answering 3 and 4 suggests checking the transition from factors to solutions. Answering 2 and 6 suggests checking the pair’s sum and product. Each response selects a useful follow-up question. Fresh answers determine the next step; a single mistake does not become a permanent diagnosis.

The teaching payoff is visible. In the interactive replay, changing a proposed pair changes the expanded expression. A learner sees 2 × 6 match 12 while 2 + 6 fails to match 7. Another interaction shows how one zero factor makes a product zero. Fraction bars, rate models, distribution examples, and labelled graphs make other ideas actionable.

The result continues beyond that explanation. Focused Khan clips and exercises connect to fresh application, a saved reviewer, and a later Rematch with new numbers. A finite session can shrink when a step needs more attention. Demonstrated understanding allows the learner to move on.

Shared quiz packs, source-linked personal note cards, same-screen study turns, and a bookmark companion support continued use. A short public challenge enters the same mapped learning experience, so discovery can become useful study.
We will test the added value of this connected package against similar-time teacher-selected Khan practice. The innovation lies in how the parts work together around the learner’s current need.

sections.name: Meaningful Khan Academy Integration
paragraphs: Dunlo is a study companion for Khan Academy. A learner can begin with a supported Khan lesson or exercise, paste a recognized activity URL, or open its shared pack. The selected Khan learning goal organizes the checks, support, practice, and next review.

Each supported pack has an explicit mapping to official Khan learning and exercises. Those resources appear within the pack and session. Official videos can play a reviewed segment, including the 2:22–3:56 factoring example, with replay and continued watching. Original interactive explanations and note cards remain clearly distinguished from Khan content.

The complete cycle is: current Khan goal, useful check or explanation, relevant Khan practice, saved return to Dunlo, fresh independent application, and scheduled review. Learners who demonstrate understanding can move on; a quick review need not force another video or exercise visit.

After Khan practice, learners can report completion, continued difficulty, or an access problem. The report changes the proposed support or next check. Fresh answers supply separate evidence of application. Resource opens, learner reports, teacher-confirmed Khan activity, and independent checks remain distinct records.

For the school routine, teachers assign matched exercises through their existing Khan classes and consult authorized assignment reports alongside learner return records. The current workflow supports manual teacher confirmation. Any CSV adapter will follow inspection of an actual permitted export and its fields.

Reels, shared challenges, and existing Khan learners converge on these same packs. The pilot will examine repeated relevant Khan assignments across teaching weeks together with useful return, learning, and teacher effort.

sections.name: Potential to Scale
paragraphs: The unit of replication is a reviewed study pack and its teaching routine. A pack connects a current goal, skill relationships, useful checks, explanations, official Khan resources, fresh applications, and review. An educator kit adds assignment instructions, assessment forms, and reporting definitions.

Dunlo’s nine destinations across mathematics, chemistry and physics demonstrate this structure, with science routes descending into the mathematics they rest on. Learners can combine supported topics, add quiz dates, and create source-linked personal note cards. Educators can reuse shared scope while each learner receives their own support and reviewer. New graded question families enter through content review and maintained mappings.

School adoption begins with one current lesson and a recurring study window. We will measure how a second educator sets up the pack, interprets the action sheet, and continues the routine without the student team directing each session. Review time, onboarding effort, and ongoing support are part of the scale model.

A complementary public channel connects original short mathematics content to exact challenge codes. Twelve planned variants cover factors, fractions, and ratios with different audience hooks. Each entry can lead into an explanation, relevant Khan activity, saved pack, and another session or share. Public acquisition and school evaluation will be reported separately.

The interface supports mobile and desktop use, text explanations, saved progress, and shared-device clearing. Same-screen group study and scope links lower the effort needed to involve classmates. Longer-term service work can add synchronized circles while retaining the existing learning records and reviewed content model.
Expansion requires a named content owner, an access arrangement, and recurring support funding. The March handover will document the cost and practical steps of replicating the routine.

sections.name: Potential Positive Impact
paragraphs: By March 31, 2027, we aim to establish whether Dunlo helps learners use Khan Academy more meaningfully and return to current mathematics work with understanding that lasts.

The primary recovery outcome is retained reentry: eligible learners who could not complete the baseline task meet a prespecified criterion on both a fresh immediate assessment and a parallel assessment 7–14 days later. The denominator includes all enrolled eligible baseline-blocked learners; missing follow-up stays visible.

Teachers will review parallel forms and supervise formal assessments. Where practical and approved, a randomized delayed-start comparison will contrast the Dunlo-supported package with similar-time teacher-selected Khan practice, using comparable access, support, and the same assessment policy. This tests the whole study routine. Product practice records provide useful context alongside the independent evaluation.

The broader companion also serves learners who are already comfortable with the current task. We will separately measure voluntary useful return, completion of planned study sessions, personal reviewer use, and shared pack reuse. These learners will not be counted as recovered merely for using the product.

A repeated-Khan-use measure will track at least one relevant assigned exercise in three of four offered teaching weeks, using available authorized reports. We will examine this with teacher minutes, learner frustration, access barriers, and actual costs. Public views and challenge attempts will remain separate from school learning outcomes.

The proposed 80–120 learners across 2–3 cohorts will test a practical implementation. Success should leave both credible evidence and an educator kit that makes useful study, follow-up, and repeated Khan use easier to sustain.
